summary: Chilaquiles verdes: pan-fry torn corn tortillas until crisp, scramble eggs in with them, and serve in hot salsa verde, saving a few crunchy wedges for the top.
glance: 1 cup salsa verde or green enchilada sauce
3 corn tortillas, torn into 6 wedges each and fried until well browned

summary: Homemade caraway rye crackers: a dough of rye and all-purpose flour rolled very thin between silpats, brushed with olive oil and Maldon salt, and baked at 400°F for 8-10 minutes until deep golden brown; makes about 36.
glance: 400°F for 8-10 minutes, until deep golden brown
very thin, generous olive oil and salt, baked quite brown
faq: What are the keys to good homemade crackers?

Roll them really, really thin; brush with a generous amount of olive oil and sprinkle on a generous amount of salt; and bake them until quite deeply brown. These details separate a brutish, underflavored cracker from one with a bright snap and a pop of rye, caraway and salt.
How thin should I roll the dough?
Roll each third of the dough between two silpats, or parchment cut to the size of the baking sheet, until it covers about 80% of the silpat's surface.
How long do you bake rye crackers?
At 400°F, using convection if available, until deep golden brown, about 8-10 minutes. Cool on a rack and break into random-sized crackers.
Can I make the dough by hand?
Yes. The recipe uses a stand mixer with the paddle and then the dough hook for about 8 minutes, but you can mix and knead by hand.
Why make crackers at home?
They taste fresher and better than most of what you can buy, and save a lot of money compared with the best grocery store crackers.

summary: A crispy corn-tortilla quesadilla: brush both sides with a little oil and cook on medium heat several minutes per side; this version is filled with green peppercorn pecorino, red onion and garlic and onion jam, with a goat cheese and cilantro sauce.
glance: brush both sides with oil and cook several minutes per side
faq: How do you make a quesadilla crispy?

Brush both sides with a bit of oil before putting it on a pan or griddle over medium-high heat, then let it cook plenty of time on each side. It doesn't need a lot of oil, and the tortilla ends up crispy and chewy like a fresh tortilla chip.
Does the crispy method work with flour tortillas?
The trick is for corn tortillas, which the author prefers for flavor and texture. Flour quesadillas are fine too but the author calls that a different article.
What happens if you cook a quesadilla dry?
The shell just heats up and dries out a bit, which is ok, but it ends up floppy rather than crispy.
What fillings work?
Anything: mild Monterey jack for a child, taleggio and grilled figs for a foodie. This one uses green peppercorn pecorino, red onion and Stonewall Kitchen roasted garlic and onion jam.
How do I make the goat cheese sauce?
Beat 2 tablespoons of goat cheese with a bit of water until smooth like thick yogurt, then stir in minced cilantro (bruised with your fingertips) and a bit of salt.
Is a quesadilla vegan?
As written it is vegetarian and gluten-free, but not vegan.

summary: Stir-fry browned tofu with asparagus and red bell pepper in Guilin chili sauce, a fermented soybean and hot chili condiment; the vegetable stir-frying takes about 2 minutes. Serves 4 over rice.
glance: 4 as a main course with rice
asparagus 1 minute, red pepper about 1 more, sauce 30 seconds
2 tablespoons Guilin chili sauce mixed with 1/4 cup water
Vegetarian and vegan; the sauce is not gluten-free
yield: 4 as a main course with rice
faq: What is Guilin chili sauce?

A famous chili sauce from Guilin, a city in southern China, where it is considered one of the city's three treasures along with a rice liquor and pickled tofu. It contains fermented soybeans combined with a very hot, fruity chili pepper.
What can I substitute for Guilin chili sauce?
For a rough approximation, use half regular black bean paste and half red chili paste such as sambal oelek or sriracha, with some garlic and a bit of sugar.
Where do I find Guilin chili sauce?
The author uses the Lee Kum Kee brand, available at Uwajimaya in Seattle or on Amazon.
How do you get the tofu well browned?

Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over a very high flame, toss in 1 pound of patted-dry extra-firm tofu and fry, tossing occasionally, until well browned on all sides. Remove to paper towels leaving as much oil behind as possible.
How hot is the dish?
Use 2 tablespoons of sauce if you like it 3-stars hot, and more if you are a 5-star person.
Is this recipe gluten-free?
It is vegetarian and vegan, but the sauce is not gluten-free.

summary: Vegetarian frijoles charros: whole pinto beans in a smoky tomato broth, with the smoke coming from a quickly smoked diced onion instead of bacon; the finished beans simmer about 15 minutes.
glance: 4 cups home-cooked pinto beans plus 2 cups of their cooking liquid
faq: What are frijoles charros?
A classic Mexican way of serving beans. Unlike refried beans, the pinto beans are served whole, in a broth redolent of smoke and tomato. Traditionally the smoke comes from bacon.
How does the vegetarian version get its smoky flavor?

By quickly smoking a diced onion over wood chips, which gives bright, volatile smoky notes that chipotle or chile moro can lack. The author's note says he no longer recommends jury-rigged stovetop smoking because of high levels of carcinogens in a low-oxygen sealed environment, and points to his Smoked Tofu Buns recipe for a safer alternative.
Should I soak wood chips before smoking?
No. The author learned from Modernist Cuisine that the best flavors come out in smoke between about 400 and 750°F, and soaked chips stay cooler and give more acrid, off flavors.
Can I use canned beans?
In a pinch, yes: thoroughly rinsed canned beans, with a good, clear vegetable broth in place of the bean cooking liquid. Home-cooked beans give a better texture and a flavorful liquid for the broth.
What do you serve with frijoles charros?
Use them as an alternative to refried beans with any Mexican meal, such as arroz verde, arroz a la Mexicana, grilled pepper and tofu tacos, enchiladas or tamales.

summary: Mandu, Korean-style potstickers filled with tofu, tempeh, blanched bean sprouts, green onion and egg, pan-fried and steamed in the pan, served with a kochujang, ssamjang and black vinegar dipping sauce; makes about 40.
glance: about 40 dumplings (serves 4-5 in the author's family)
60-90 seconds until golden, then steam with about 3 tablespoons of water for about 3 minutes
tofu, tempeh, bean sprouts, green onion, egg
faq: What is mandu?
The generic name for Korean dumplings, sometimes spelled mandoo. Panfried ones are gunmandu, and vegetarian dumplings are somandu.
What is in the vegetarian mandu filling?

Blanched mung bean sprouts, crumbled and squeezed tofu, pan-fried crumbled tempeh, green onions, garlic, tamari and sesame oil, bound with beaten egg. The egg binds the filling into a slightly fluffy but firm bite.
How do I get a tight seal on potstickers?
Don't overfill: about 2 teaspoons of filling per wrapper, moisten the edge, fold and seal firmly. The author found a simple dumpling press made pleating and sealing easy, even for his child.
How do you pan-fry mandu?

Fry in a large skillet over medium-high heat with 2 tablespoons of oil, pleats up and not touching, for about 60-90 seconds until golden on the bottom. Add about 3 tablespoons of water, lower the heat, cover and cook about 3 minutes, then uncover and cook off any excess water.
What is the dipping sauce?

Whisk 1/4 cup kochujang, 1/3 cup ssamjang and 1/3 cup black vinegar, adding water to reach a dipping consistency. Black vinegar replaces the sherry vinegar in the Momofuku-inspired sauce and has a slight five-spice flavor.
Where do I find kochujang and ssamjang?
At a Korean grocery or a well-stocked general Asian grocery.

summary: A vegetarian spaghetti alla carbonara: garlic and spicy pickled Mama Lil's peppers in a skillet, tossed with pasta and then aggressively with eggs, Parmigiano and black pepper, topped with toasted pine nuts and parsley.
glance: 1/2 cup Mama Lil's peppers, with their oil

summary: Thai basil eggplant: Asian eggplant cubes stir-fried with ginger, garlic and smashed lemongrass, steamed briefly with a little water, then finished with mushrooms, onion, chili and a big bunch of Thai basil.
glance: 2 as a main course, 4 as part of a larger spread
stir-fry about 1 minute, steam, then about 1 minute with the basil
faq: What is Thai basil?

The herb called Thai basil has purplish stems and green leaves. Holy basil is a different, much-loved Thai herb with purple leaves and an incredible aroma. Both are quite different from Italian basil, which the author wouldn't use here.
Why use Thai basil in a cooked dish?
It stands up to a good amount of cooking, so it can be used almost as a vegetable, not just a garnish, though a few leaves are reserved to garnish.
What eggplant works best?
Asian eggplant, like the long Japanese ones about 1 1/2 inches in diameter. The texture isn't quite right with an Italian-type eggplant.
Do I need a wok?
A wok works fine without a jet-powered burner because you aren't trying to brown the eggplant, but a large skillet also works.
How do you prepare lemongrass?

Trim all but the last 4 inches or so of the stem end and trim the hard button off. Remove the outermost layer or two, smash the piece with something heavy, like a can of beans, until tenderized, then mince.
Is it a main course or a side dish?
It serves 2 as a main course or 4 as part of a larger spread. The author wouldn't have it alone with jasmine rice, but it can stand next to a dish like red curry delicata squash and tofu.

summary: Five-minute Indian-style cabbage: black mustard seeds popped in hot oil, a few quick spices, then sliced green cabbage stir-fried until crisp-tender; it comes together in 5 minutes.
glance: 1 tablespoon black mustard seeds, cumin, turmeric, cayenne
faq: What flavors go with cabbage in Indian cooking?
Everything in the cabbage (brassica) family goes great with mustard, so mustard seeds are the primary flavoring here.
Can I use mustard oil?
Yes. If you have mustard oil, use it instead of the vegetable oil and reduce the mustard seeds by half.
How do you temper the mustard seeds?

Heat the oil over medium-high heat, wait 10 seconds, add the mustard seeds, and as soon as they pop add the rest of the spices and stir-fry 10 more seconds. Move quickly so the oil is infused but the spices don't burn, with everything chopped and measured in advance.
What optional additions work?
Garlic, ginger, unsweetened shredded coconut, fresh chilis or dried chili flakes and garam masala, with cilantro and lemon juice to garnish.
What do I serve it with?
The author makes it when serving a curry, rice and raita and wanting one more dish to round out an Indian meal.

summary: Apio is a Sephardic lemony celery root side dish: celery root and carrot simmered in lemon juice, olive oil, sugar and salt for about 30 minutes covered, then until tender, with the liquid reduced by half; served warm or chilled.
glance: warm or chilled, with good bread to mop up the liquid
faq: What is apio?

Apio is celery root (celeriac) in Ladino, the Judeo-Spanish language of the author's wife's Sephardic relatives, who like lemony foods. Here it is simmered in lemony water until tender and the liquid reduces to a thin sauce.
How do you cook apio?

Combine the sliced celery root, carrot, olive oil, juice of 2 lemons, sugar and salt in a saucepan with just enough water to barely cover. Boil, then simmer covered for 30 minutes, uncover and cook until the celery root is completely tender. Move the vegetables to a bowl and boil the liquid until it reduces by about half.
Should apio be served hot or cold?
Warm or chilled. The author likes it best cold, with good artisanal bread to mop up every drop.
How thick is the sauce?
It won't be thick like a sauce, but it will have a slight body to it.
What does apio go with?
It is a simple side dish that goes well with entrees based on cheese or pastry, because the bright lemony flavor cuts through any heaviness.
